strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Journey admission can be retried safely after late checkpoint or journey-start event commit failure without orphan task ambiguity.
Rust owns the admission preflight, conflict checks, rollback, and replay behavior before returning a bounded result.

The runtime keeps journey checkpoint and HeadlessJourneyStarted evidence consistent with the admitted task/run or removes the partial task/run on commit failure before the agent loop can advance from ambiguous admission state.
Failure and replay evidence remains bounded to ids, state classes, and fingerprints without exposing raw task content or ledger payloads.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and context_management.
answers.new_capability: A journey admission now rolls back the just-created task/run when checkpoint persistence fails and rolls back both checkpoint and task/run when HeadlessJourneyStarted event commit fails, so retry can start cleanly without duplicate tasks.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M50.1 delegated to task.start before journey checkpoint persistence, leaving a documented failure window where a filesystem error could create an orphan task without journey replay evidence.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless callers could still receive a failed admission after task creation and later retry into ambiguous progress state with no journey checkpoint binding the orphan task.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M53.2 continuation freshness, M54.1 debt carry-forward admission, and M54.2 debt state transitions because it changes the journey admission side-effect boundary.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase changes existing headless.run.drive journey admission behavior only.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It adds no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, registry, or summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust cleans up partial journey admission side effects after late checkpoint/event failures and preserves existing exact replay/conflict behavior for committed admissions.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A scheduled controller can retry a failed journey start without external orphan-task reconciliation or manual state surgery.
answers.milestone_progress: Resolves the carried M50.1 admission atomicity debt and makes M55 closeout-assessable.

exit_criteria: checkpoint persistence failure after task creation removes the just-created task/run and leaves no journey checkpoint
HeadlessJourneyStarted event commit failure removes the matching journey checkpoint and just-created task/run
retry after either late failure creates exactly one committed journey admission
successful journey admission replay remains exact and does not duplicate task, checkpoint, drive, or journey evidence
conflicting replay is still denied before new side effects
no new RPC or wrapper/report/readiness surface is added
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_checkpoint_failure_rolls_back_started_task forces checkpoint path failure and verifies rollback plus clean retry
Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_started_event_failure_rolls_back_checkpoint_and_task simulates journey-start event failure and verifies checkpoint/task rollback plus clean retry
Existing Rust journey admission replay and conflicting replay tests continue to cover exact replay and no duplicate task creation

accepted_capability: Runtime atomic headless journey admission checkpoint behavior
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-runtime headless_run_drive_journey -- --nocapture covers rollback, replay, invalid admission, and conflict behavior
safety_boundary: reuses existing headless.run.drive and task.start authority
rolls back only the just-created task/run after matching task_id/run_id verification
removes only the matching journey checkpoint
does not expose raw prompts, file content, diffs, stdout/stderr, commands, environment, paths, or secrets
rejected_alternatives: external orphan cleanup by the controller
broad store transaction abstraction as the deliverable
technical_debt: The rollback is scoped to journey admission; later route-resume atomicity should only be planned if a concrete partial-boundary gap is found.
Runtime lib.rs remains large and should not displace capability work unless it blocks safe changes.
next_capability_rationale: If M55.1 is accepted, M55 should be closeout-assessable because the carried M50.1 journey admission atomicity debt is resolved with runtime rollback behavior instead of a report or controller cleanup wrapper.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M55.1 updates current and archived phase-value manifests for a runtime journey-admission atomicity phase. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and no wrapper/report/readiness surface was added.
